note: What the Screamsheet says, and in whose voice. The facts are the engine's — a flag a place gained, what a settled job left behind — and every line here is a template over one of them. NOTHING IN THIS FILE MAY ADD A FACT: atmosphere may colour what happened ("they know the address now"), but it may not say what nobody recorded (a name, a sum, who said what, what police announced). A line that names the character does so only when the engine says somebody said their name (`named`) or, for fame, from Reputation 5, where the printed ladder first says the name is out (Level 4 is only stories, so it reads "a runner"). Tokens: {place} the venue, {handle} the character's handle, {count} how many, {who} the character's handle or 'a runner', {ladder} the Reputation line printed on p.193. A template is picked from its list by a hash of the event, so it reads the same every time the sheet is opened. Fame is printed from Reputation 3: at 1 and 2 only the people who were there, and their friends, know, and that is not news.
